title: Update: Muay Thai game
author: Wild-Elevator6639
selftext:
Hey y'all,

A couple of days ago I posted asking for help creating a Muay Thai fighting game. Just wanted to give an update on where I'm at after hitting my weekly limit with Astra. Just for reference, I have zero coding ability.

I used Nano Banana to create video game renderings of two fighters and then had Tripo create models and rig them. Did the same with the arena. Then I had Astra refine the rigging and import the assets into Unity. I purchased some animation packs from the Unity store and cobbled together the fighters' moveset with those and some downloads from Mixamo. The rest of the credits were spent smoothing out movements.

The goal here is to build as realistic a game as possible. I could use some feedback on things like smoothing out movements, improving graphics and refining collision. Any other feedback is also welcome.

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Hey! Alex here from the Tripo Studio US team. This is a huge jump from the first post.

For zero coding experience, getting two fighters, an arena, rigging, Unity import, and a working moveset together this quickly is pretty wild.

For realism, I’d probably focus next on animation blending, hit reactions, and collision timing before polishing graphics too much. Muay Thai will really live or die on whether the weight transfer and contact feel believable.

Curious which part feels weakest to you right now: the strikes themselves, transitions between moves, or how the fighters react on contact?
